sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Pulls in the Tailwind framework and two shared style files.
sections.why: Needed so the page has the framework and shared looks.
sections.watch_out: Order matters: shared files load after the framework, so their rules can override it.

sections.name: :root
sections.title: Base colours and font variable
sections.what: Sets the default background, text and accent colours, a faint panel tint, a border colour, and the font variable.
sections.why: Likely reason: one place to change the main colours.
sections.watch_out: Changing the accent colour also changes shadows and buttons that use it.

sections.name: html
sections.title: Framework colour mapping and fonts
sections.what: Redirects the framework's black and red names to the brand palette and sets both sans and mono fonts to one family.
sections.why: The comments say there is no pure black or red, and the monospace look is retired.
sections.watch_out: Any red or black class now uses brand shades, so a new pure colour needs an explicit value.

sections.name: body
sections.title: Page root behaviour
sections.what: Makes in-page links scroll smoothly, leaves room at the top for a fixed header, and controls text size on phones.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed header would otherwise hide section headings.
sections.watch_out: The 84 pixel top padding is fixed, so a taller header will overlap headings.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
sections.title: Body margin and font
sections.what: Removes the default page margin and sets the body font.
sections.why: Likely reason: consistent page edges and font.

sections.name: .app-dark
sections.title: Reduced motion rule
sections.what: Turns off smooth scrolling for users who asked for less motion.
sections.why: Likely reason: accessibility for people sensitive to movement.

sections.name: .glass-panel
sections.title: Dark app shell (legacy)
sections.what: Gives a dark background with faint grid lines to older dark app pages.
sections.why: The comment says it is the existing shell and will be redesigned in Phase 1.
sections.watch_out: It is marked as temporary, so it may be removed later.

sections.name: .neo-brutal
sections.title: Glass panel
sections.what: A frosted panel with blur, a thin border and a dark shadow.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared panel look for cards.
sections.watch_out: Heavy blur can slow older phones.

sections.name: .neo-brutal:hover
sections.title: Neo-brutal card hover state
sections.what: On hover the card moves 2px down and right and its hard shadow shrinks to a 2px offset in the accent colour.
sections.why: Makes the card look pressed in when hovered.
sections.watch_out: The base card style and any transition are defined elsewhere, not in these lines.

sections.name: .neo-brutal:active
sections.title: Neo-brutal hover and press
sections.what: Moves the card slightly and shrinks its shadow on hover, then pushes it in when pressed.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a pressed-button feel.
sections.watch_out: The hover and press offsets are fixed pixel values and must stay in step with the base shadow.

summary: The main stylesheet: imports shared styles, sets base colours and fonts, and defines a few reusable looks.
purpose: Sets the site-wide look, including colours, font, page background and motion settings.
why: The comments give reasons for the colour mapping and the single font. Other reasons are not stated.
how: Imports the framework and shared files, defines base colours and the font, maps the framework's black and red names to brand colours, sets smooth scrolling that turns off for reduced motion, and defines panel and button looks.
inputs: Shared token and component files and theme variables.
outputs: Colours, fonts and the reusable look classes used across the site.
risks: Remapping red and black changes every use of those framework classes. The old monospace font is retired, so older pages may look different.
debug: If colours look wrong, check the mapping block and the token file. If a font is missing, check the font variable.
